title: The Largest XOR of the Road Values Along a Walk

concept.title: Any walk is a tree path plus some cycles; the cycle values form an XOR basis, and a greedy pass picks the best combination
body: Towns are connected by two-way roads, each road with a value. A **walk** from the town 1 to the town `n` may use any road any number of times (also going back), and its value is the **XOR** of the values of the roads used, each time it is used. Find the largest possible value. A road used twice cancels itself (`w xor w = 0`), which is the key to the problem.

Take any spanning tree (a BFS tree) and let `d[v]` be the XOR of the values on the tree path from the town 1 to `v`. Every walk from 1 to `n` has the value `d[n]` xor the XOR of some **cycles** that the walk goes around: for a road `(u, v, w)` that is not in the tree, the cycle it closes has the value `d[u] xor d[v] xor w` (for a tree road this is 0). Every combination of cycles is possible, because a walk can go to a cycle, go around it and come back along the same road (which cancels). So the set of reachable values is `d[n] xor (any XOR of cycle values)`.

body.code:
for u, v, w in edges:                       # tree edges give 0 and are skipped by the insert
    x = d[u] ^ d[v] ^ w
    for b in range(29, -1, -1):             # insert x into the xor basis
        if x >> b & 1:
            if basis[b] == 0: basis[b] = x; break
            x ^= basis[b]
res = d[n]
for b in range(29, -1, -1):
    if res ^ basis[b] > res: res ^= basis[b]     # greedy: the highest bit decides

body: An **XOR basis** keeps at most 30 numbers with distinct highest bits that generate all combinations of the inserted numbers. To get the maximum of `res xor (combination)`, go from the highest bit down and use the basis vector for the bit `b` whenever it increases the result. The BFS and the 100000 insertions cost O(n + 30 m) in total.

statement: `n` towns are connected by `m` two-way roads; the road `i` joins `u` and `v` and has the value `w`. A walk may use any road any number of times, in any direction. The value of a walk is the XOR of the values of all the roads it uses, counted every time a road is used. Find the largest value of a walk that starts in the town 1 and ends in the town `n`.
inputFormat: The first line has `n` and `m`: the number of towns and the number of roads.
Each of the next `m` lines has three numbers `u`, `v` and `w`: a two-way road between the towns `u` and `v` with the value `w`.
outputFormat: Print one number: the largest value.
constraints: The towns are connected. Roads can repeat, and u can equal v.

examples.note: The walk 1-2-4 has the value 3 xor 5 = 6, and the walk 1-3-4 has 6 xor 1 = 7. The cycle through all four roads has the value 1, so 7 is the best.

hints: Using a road twice cancels it, so a walk is a path plus any set of cycles.
With a BFS tree, the cycle closed by an edge (u, v, w) has the value d[u] xor d[v] xor w.
Put the cycle values in an XOR basis and maximise d[n] xor (combination) greedily from the highest bit.

starter.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, m = map(int, input().split())
edges = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(m)]

explanation: A BFS tree gives d[v], the XOR of the tree path from the town 1. Every non-tree road closes a cycle of value d[u] xor d[v] xor w, and these values go into an XOR basis. The best walk value is d[n] improved greedily from the highest bit with the basis.
solution.complexity: Time O(n + 30 m), space O(n + m).
